candidate_evidence.finding: Original workflow contains the exact sg shell pipeline ending || true; 406 is its unmodified first stage. All-row grep claude- is broader than anchored instance-name matching, cut chooses first CSV field and xargs -r -n1 invokes force-delete separately per item. Official Incus list supports CSV and configured project/remote inventory; delete --force removes running instances. Maintainer fix patch reports active sessions destroyed by test cleanup and changes workflow selector. Source text does not establish this exact workflow was executed.

Historical pre-wiki-migration README explicitly shows coi kill --all --force under Kill all without confirmation; same-revision MIT license inspected. It is a published Bash example, not reconstruction from argv or a wiki-license assumption. Existing 322 provides safe container/session inventory. No assumption that all Coi sessions are disposable.

Both official snapshot examples verified; machine reset stops all running machines, deletes all machines, configuration and data including VM diskimages and previously pulled cache images; --force skips confirmation. Machine-list .md.in has literal podman machine list with default table name/type/created/last-up/CPU/memory/disk-size metadata, no private-key content. Rootless machine-management scope differs from native engine storage reset.

MIT consumer README Development starts DragonflyDB and Orthanc services for testing, optionally fetches sample data, then gives literal podman-compose down -v under Clean up. No data samples collected. Independent current implementation confirms down stops/removes service containers, optionally removes project-labeled volumes, then pods/networks; volume_ls filters io.podman.compose.project. Version in consumer unknown: do not promise all Dockerfile anonymous volumes are found, external volumes removed, data safe, or cleanup succeeded. Current GPL implementation used only as behavioral corroboration, not redistributed command source.

Exact retry loop occurs inside sudo bash body, after explicit DATA LOSS WARNING/selector and service-stop steps. Only the existing standalone loop is extracted; surrounding confirmation/service shutdown/privilege are not part of accepted command, so there is no preapproved authorization. On failure until sleeps one second then retries, potentially indefinitely while runtime continues producing/rejecting sandboxes. stdout alone is hidden; stderr remains. Official pinned rmp all selects all sandboxes and force stops READY before RemovePodSandbox. Local runtime sandbox cleanup belongs CAT-3.3, not a Kubernetes API cluster/namespace deletion.

Pinned official crictl guide contains literal crictl pods and sample READY sandbox output. It lists pod sandbox metadata independently of dangerous source; not identical to crictl ps -a ordinary-container listing.

independent_label_decision.405: deny/high is tied to a specific confirmed unintended-target cleanup pattern: repository owner reports active sessions killed and fixes this selector. It is not deny merely because incus delete deletes, and not an invented production rule. Matching all CSV fields plus forced running-instance deletion supports the unsafe-target scenario; sg changes group for the shell pipeline and || true masks aggregate failure, neither makes it safe.
independent_label_decision.407_408_410_411: ask independently requires owner responsibility for active-container teardown, VM-disk/state loss, project data-volume removal, or all-runtime sandbox disruption. The source examples and internal/outer source confirmation do not authorize a new invocation. This is not automatic modify-to-ask. Development/test origin does not establish present state expendability.
independent_label_decision.severity: 408 critical is justified by all machine hosts/configurations and VM disk-image destruction; other destructive rows high reflect broad session/runtime/project state loss or intervention. No unsupported backup/recovery/production claim.
independent_label_decision.allow: 406/409/412 are metadata listings without starting/stopping/removing workloads, reading content/keys/logs or writing files. They are independently safe under documented normal trusted-client operation. 406 is a source-stage extraction, not generated command construction. Listing does not authorize future deletion.
